content: This channel is for discussion of Tau Ceti, the library of formal mathematics incubated by the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, written by AIs following human reviewed roadmaps.

(This channel is initially private as we do some preparations for launch. Do note that I intend that this channel will become public upon launch: please speak with that in mind! If there is a need for a long-term private coordination channel, ask me via DM and I'll set that up.)

I've pre-populated a few topics to try to get the conversation organized:

  • #Tau Ceti > Getting started: making a PR
  • #Tau Ceti > Getting started: roadmaps
  • #Tau Ceti > Getting started: reviewing
  • #Tau Ceti > Getting started: the tauceti CLI
  • #Tau Ceti > Getting started: reviewing current content
  • #Tau Ceti > Possible next steps
@channel, welcome!
Is this meant to be a private channel (but a public repo)? I didn’t read.
Awesome! Thanks creating this, @Kim Morrison!

This looks like a great project, thanks for setting it up. I have several roadmaps that I've been working through which I'm happy to contibute. One quick question, when it comes to making PRs, can they have sorries? I couldn't see this mentioned, but maybe the answer is no because CI will fail?
Or maybe I just can't read and just missed this!
PRs to the main repository may not use sorry. PRs to the TauCetiRoadmap repository may be a mix of markdown and Lean, and the Lean files can use sorry or def_wanted/theorem_wanted however you like!

I've read the "Mathlib dependency" section in the readme and I'm not sure to understand the sentence

For now we depend on Mathlib's master branch. AIs are encouraged to make PRs that bump the pin to new commits on the master branch, and fix any resulting problems in the library.

in the sense that it can be read as "AI's are encouraged to bump Mathlib constantly and if there are problems to try to fix the Mathlib library" (although the final "library" is meant to be TauCeti, I suppose)
Oh! I find it hard to bend that text to any reading that suggests interacting with Mathlib, but if anyone would like to suggest a rewrite of that sentence, I'll take it.

I was suggesting something simple like avoiding repeating "library" when two are at stake:

For now we depend on Mathlib's master branch. AIs are encouraged to make PRs to TauCeti that bump the pin to new commits on Mathlib's master branch, and suggest fixing TauCeti whenever problems resulting from the bump should occur.
Hooray!
5 messages were moved from this topic to #Tau Ceti > Naming the project by Kim Morrison.

Just a heads up that I'm am going to be mostly-offline from now until July 18. I will try to leave some workers running doing reviews and PRs, but they will probably break without my supervision, so please expect some interruptions to service. It should be perfectly possible for others to keep things going, as described in #Tau Ceti > Getting started: the tauceti CLI , merely by running

uv tool install git+https://github.com/kim-em/TauCetiWorker.git
tauceti work --loop --host --only review

(to keep a reviewer going indefinitely; --host means don't run in a sandbox; you can try with or without, but please use appropriate precautions) or tauceti work --loop --host if you'd also like your agents to fix and submit PRs according to the roadmaps.

I have tried this afternoon (and will continue working until I leave) to get the PR queue unstuck fully, and the roadmap PRs reviewed or merged. Please also continue submitting and reviewing roadmaps!

I'm hoping that we will "go live" shortly after I'm back online.

Hi, @Kim Morrison .
Can Lean Pool also get its own channel under the Projects folder? Since it's a similar project to TauCeti, it seems reasonable. We have the same number of contributors as TauCeti and are aiming to expand fast, similar to TauCeti. As we discussed, the two projects have little overlap, so there should not be much contention. Btw, I added a small comparison to Lean Pool's README about TauCeti: https://github.com/Vilin97/lean-pool#difference-from-similar-projects.

Thanks!
Done: #Lean Pool > channel events @ 💬

Hi, I'm new to Tau Ceti, but I have two naive questions.

  • What should we do to results that are definitely intended to be put on mathlib, but are not yet in a mathlib PR because we want things to get done quickly and it's needed for other things? Obviously I cannot edit a mathlib file directly, so should there be a unified ForMathlib folder?
  • I guess this is more for Lean Pool and other arXiv-like Lean repos, but is there a good way to check that statements we formalise are semantically faithful, other than just trusting adversarial AI reviews? For instance, for each project proving a result, can we have a "Defs.lean" file and a "Theorems.lean" file using only stuff from "Defs.lean", so users who want to use the repo only have to look at these two files and nothing else in between?

No, please don't make a ForMathlib folder. Just put things where they go in TauCeti/, and we'll delete/replace/refactor when they later appear in Mathlib.

So far, I've been thinking that semantic alignment is something we should build as a separate layer, that works across repositories. There's some existing discussion at #Tau Ceti > Auditing definitions , but we need to have people writing prototypes to get off the ground.

Announcement: Tau Ceti now has docgen. This is regenerated daily, rather than every commit to main.

Note that Github Pages website limits sites to 1gb, and Mathlib docgen is getting very close to this by itself, so downstream projects will start breaking soon. To solve this, I've opened a PR https://github.com/leanprover/doc-gen4/pull/396 to doc-gen4 allowing you to link to an existing doc-gen site for an upstream dependency, and the Tau Ceti docgen pages use this. Everything it still cross-linked to Mathlib docs, but there may be occasional slight inconsistencies because they aren't generated/updated simultaneously.

Thanks and great work putting this together
Yep if its getting past the AI reviewers that means it looks good :)
